U.note: Taxonomic-record form with etymology and a sheep-ledger first record is grounded and usable, but the chatty preamble and flat tone hold it back.

V.note: Well-organised guide with tables and the ember seam as a nice mark, yet the cinder dragon with similar-species list is fairly stock.

W.note: A wingless, Komodo-scaled fell wyrm with band-count individual ID and a bluff display is coherent, well-sourced and compact.

X.note: Competent but leans on stock dragon tropes (hoards, thermals, buckle in scat) with little new.

Y.note: Fjord wyrm known by sign first, with seasonal table, sealers' lore and vivid measurements set beside familiar objects; rich, though long.

Z.note: Opens with the burn line and shed skin and works back to the animal, with honest unknowns about winter; clever and usable.
